pr_body:

Add details of changes here.
- Extends the import/export command in About page to all settings. Settings are exported in a .zip file. It includes: pinned items, user settings, file tags, terminal profiles, bundles. On import, all settings are applied without restart.

issue_context.title: Save favorites in the settings json
issue_context.body:
### Description

My files (2.0.36) has vertical tabs button off but when importing to files (2.0.39) it gets turned on again. Side bar pins and home screen widgets don't get saved or applied if they are saved.

### Steps To Reproduce

_No response_

### Expected behavior

It should correctly apply/save settings stated above

### Files Version

2.0.39.0

### Windows Version

10.0.19043.1348

### Relevant Assets

[debug.log](https://github.com/files-community/Files/files/7582928/debug.log)
[debug_fulltrust.log](https://github.com/files-community/Files/files/7582929/debug_fulltrust.log)
comments: The sidebar favorites are considered settings and are stored in a different file but perhaps we can merge them into the settings file.
@gave92 that's a great idea! I think we can remove the terminal settings and default to the system terminal.

Do you mean merging them only when exporting or also in the app? If we merged the terminal profile with the main settings, clicking on "Edit Terminals" would open a file full of stuff not related to terminals.

> Do you mean merging them only when exporting or also in the app? If we merged the terminal profile with the main settings, clicking on "Edit Terminals" would open a file full of stuff not related to terminals.

@gave92 I edited my original message.
@josh-65 this issue should be resolved with #7078.

review_comments: No need, FilesystemResult is useful only if we care about why the call has failed. Here we really don't.
Will it throw if the json is invalid?
Yeah but we have a catch in AboutViewModel. In any case I'll make this method coherent with the other ImportSettings methods.
Actually most other ImportSettings() methods (e.g. UserSettings) don't do exception handling, keeping like this for now. The catch in AboutViewModel should be enough.
Should we drop v1 and just stick with v2 while at it?
@yaichenbaum should we drop support for old "PinnedItems.txt"? Don't quite remember how old is that.
Not removed, but given priority to V2 which is what 99% of users will have.
